text: {"headline":"Timesheet Review: Weekend Dispatch Overtime Hours Adjustment March-April 2026","overview":"This brief summarizes documented timesheet submissions, edits, and related records for the weekend dispatch team based only on the supplied calibrated claims. It presents the sequence of entries and adjustments, recorded financial totals, and conflicting documentation without drawing conclusions about intent or liability.","key_points":["On 4 March 2026, Nima Brack submitted 48 overtime hours for the weekend dispatch team [C001].","Two days later, PERSON_1 PERSON_1 removed 18 overtime hours from the approved timesheets without employee sign-off [C002].","The following Monday, Nima Brack challenged the missing overtime in the payroll queue [C004], and after the audit exported the timesheet revision history [C005].","In early April, PERSON_1 authorized repayment of six of the removed overtime hours [C003].","The agreed overtime rate is $24 per hour [C006]; the original 48 hours total $1,152 [C007], while the edited 30 hours total $720, a $432 difference corresponding to 18 hours [C008, C016].","Six hours were restored for $144, leaving 12 hours or $288 in dispute [C009, C017].","The correction reason field contains only budget alignment [C010] and employee approvals are blank [C011].","Gate scans and loading manifests cover all three shifts [C012], though a gate scan does not itself establish paid working time [C013].","PERSON_1 PERSON_1's payroll memo alleges all 18 removed hours were duplicate clock entries [C014], which conflicts with records showing coverage for all three shifts, with uncertainty noted about what gate scans prove.","No signed audit report was available for this packet [C015]."],"risk_notes":["Documentation gaps include blank employee approvals and a correction reason limited to budget alignment, with no signed audit report available to independently verify the adjustment.","Conflicting accounts exist between the payroll memo allegation of duplicate entries and records indicating gate scans and manifests cover all three shifts, while gate scans alone do not establish paid working time."],"limitations":["The evidence does not show intent behind the removal or the meaning of budget alignment beyond the text in the correction field.","The evidence does not independently prove whether the 18 hours were duplicate entries or valid overtime, and does not establish that gate scans or manifests equate to paid working time.","The evidence does not include a signed audit report or employee sign-off records for the edited timesheets.","Date precision is limited for several events described as the following Monday, in early April, and after the audit."]}
